summary: Cartwright Airport (YRF/CYCA) is a small regional airport serving the remote coastal community of Cartwright in Labrador, Canada, situated along Sandwich Bay on the Labrador Sea. The airport provides a vital transportation link for residents of this isolated outport community, which has historical roots as a fishing settlement and Moravian mission site. It primarily handles regional turboprop flights connecting Cartwright to larger hubs in Newfoundland and Labrador.
faqs:
Q: How do I get to Cartwright Airport?
A: The airport is located on the eastern edge of Cartwright town, accessible by a short drive along the local road network. There is no public transit, so arranging a rental car or taxi in advance is recommended.

Q: What airlines fly into Cartwright Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional carriers operating turboprop aircraft, typically providing scheduled connections to Goose Bay and other Labrador destinations.

Q: Does the airport have facilities for passengers?
A: As a small airport serving a remote community, facilities are limited to basic terminal services. Travelers should arrive prepared and confirm services with their carrier in advance.

Q: Is there parking available at the airport?
A: Yes, the airport offers on-site parking for passengers and visitors, typical of small regional facilities in Labrador.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-arranged ground transportation are the primary ways to reach Cartwright from the airport, as the community is small and walkable but spread out. Driving from the airport into the town center takes only a few minutes along the local coastal road. Visitors planning to explore the surrounding Labrador wilderness should arrange a rental vehicle well in advance, as options are limited.
local_tip: Pack layers and windproof gear regardless of the season—Cartwright's position on the Labrador coast means weather can shift quickly, and even summer mornings can be surprisingly cold with strong sea breezes off Sandwich Bay.
